info.title: typesafe/jev-1.13.0
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "typesafe/jev-1.13.0", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Comfy Router input schema for TypeSafe Jev, the System One decision model (https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md). Send a `state` to evaluate and a map of typed `questions`; each answer comes back under the same question id. Images ride inline in `assets` and are referenced by their key anywhere in `state`, `instructions` or `criteria` (https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.md). Box questions need `typesafe/jev-1.14.0`; `typesafe/jev-1.13.0` refuses them.

example.state: Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days.

assets.description: The images in the request, keyed by a reference string. Every reference must appear somewhere in `state`, `instructions` or `criteria`. Each image is a still PNG or JPEG of 280 to 1568 pixels per side and at most 16 MiB after decoding; TypeSafe refuses a call over 32 MiB in total.

model.description: The pinned Jev version. Optional: Router fills it from the model id in the path. The `jev-latest` and `jev-preview` aliases are not accepted.

questions.description: The questions to answer, keyed by an id you choose. The answer to each is returned under the same id.

state.description: The content to evaluate: a string, or structured data (an object or array) up to 64 levels deep. An asset reference anywhere in it is replaced by that image.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description: Comfy Router output schema for TypeSafe Jev: the System One answer document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT RETURN, so the answers arrive on the original call. `answers` holds one answer per question, under the question's id; `usage` is the token count the call is billed by, images included as input tokens.

answers.description: One answer per question, keyed by the question ids you sent.

model.description: The Jev version that answered, such as `jev-1.14.0`.

input_tokens.description: Input tokens, including every image in the request.

TypesafeSystemOneAnswer.description: One answer. `type` matches the question's and decides which sibling fields are set.

box.description: For `box`, the four edges of the smallest box around the target, each a fraction from 0 to 1 of the image measured from its top-left corner: `left` and `right` of the width, `top` and `bottom` of the height. `left` is less than `right` and `top` is less than `bottom`. A box answer is always a box, even when the target is absent; ask a `noul` alongside it to check.

confidence.description: For `choice`, `score` and `box`, how certain the model is, from 0 to 1.

legend.description: For `score`, each level index mapped back to its description.

probabilities.description: For `choice`, every option mapped to its probability; for `score`, every level index. The probabilities sum to 1.

score.description: For `score`, the probability-weighted level; it can land between levels.

type.description: The question type this answers (`noul`, `choice`, `score` or `box`).

TypesafeSystemOneAsset.description: One inline image. Send the file base64-encoded in `data_base64` with its `format`.

data_base64.description: The image file, standard base64 with `=` padding, no line breaks and no `data:` prefix. The decoded bytes must be a PNG or JPEG matching `format`.

format.description: The image format, in lowercase. `jpeg` is another name for `jpg`.

type.description: The kind of asset. Optional; when sent it must be `image`.

TypesafeSystemOneQuestion.description: One typed question. `noul` is a yes/no question, `choice` picks one option from `criteria`, `score` rates along the ordered levels in `criteria`, and `box` (Jev 1.14 only, needs an image) finds where something is in an image.

criteria.description: For `noul`, optional `true`/`false` descriptions. For `choice`, a map of option name to description (at most 255 options). For `score`, an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions. `box` takes no criteria.

instructions.description: What to decide. A string, or an object or array holding the question in one field and data it refers to in others.
